title: What C# is vs JS/TS
hook: C# is a statically typed, compiled language whose types survive into IL and the CLR. TypeScript is a checker that erases; Node is a JavaScript host. Interviews fail when you treat those three as the same “runtime.”

sections.heading: Language, CTS, CLR — not Node
sections.prose: C# sits on the .NET Common Type System (CTS): every value has a type the compiler knows, and that type is written into the assembly as metadata. The common language runtime (CLR) loads that assembly, verifies it, and executes it. JavaScript engines (V8 in Node, or the Lambda Node runtime) parse source or bytecode and JIT it without a CTS contract you can share with F# or VB. TypeScript adds compile-time checking, then emits JavaScript; at run time there is no `int` versus `string` enforcement from the language. When you ship an SQS consumer as a .NET Lambda, the host is the .NET runtime (custom runtime or managed .NET Lambda), not `node`. Same AWS event, different process model, different type system, different GC. Heap layout and GC generations belong in module 14; here the point is only that the host is the CLR, not V8.

snippets.label: Types stay after compile
snippets.explanation: The compiler rejects assigning a bool to attemptCount. After publish, the CLR still sees Int32. A TS `number` would have been erased to a IEEE-754 JS number.

sections.heading: What to say in an interview
sections.prose: A clean one-liner: C# compiles to IL for the CLR; TypeScript type-checks then disappears; JavaScript is what Node executes. Productivity features (top-level statements, file-based apps) do not change that stack. If the interviewer asks why a Redis cache client in C# can share a `ConnectionMultiplexer` as a typed singleton, the answer starts with “the type is real at run time,” not “because we used TypeScript interfaces.”

interviewTakeaways: Name three layers: C# language, CTS/BCL types, CLR host.
TypeScript does not give you a CLR; Node Lambdas are a different host from .NET Lambdas.
C# is in the C family for braces and semicolons, but value types, privacy, and IL metadata are not JS semantics.
commonPitfalls: Saying C# is “just Java with a different runtime” and skipping CTS/CLR.
Assuming `tsc` is analogous to `dotnet build` — tsc erases; the C# compiler emits typed IL.
Calling the Lambda handler “Node-like” because both use JSON events. The deserializer and types are still CLR objects.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS types are compile-time only. C# types remain as metadata the CLR uses for safety, reflection, and interop.
Node executes JS on V8. A .NET worker or Lambda executes IL on the CLR. Same SQS payload, different process and type system.
